turns.user_message: I want to work from Berlin from 3 November to 14 December 2026 — can I?
turns.final_answer:
You have completed 45 months of continuous service as of 1 September 2026, which exceeds the 12-month minimum required to work outside your home country.

Your 42-day stay in Germany (3 November to 14 December) exceeds the 30-day threshold and therefore requires director approval, Tax & Legal review, and written notice at least 21 calendar days before departure.

Germany is an approved destination for temporary work abroad.

Your 42-day stay falls within the rolling 90-day annual limit for work outside your home country.

You must use a company-managed, full-disk-encrypted laptop with always-on VPN, and IT Security must be notified of your destination at least 5 business days before departure.

You may not sign contracts or negotiate customer agreements on behalf of Mosaic Robotics while abroad, and Tax & Legal review will typically approve stays over 30 days with conditions including a hard end date and prohibition on customer-facing activity.

International business travel of 30 consecutive days or fewer does not trigger Tax & Legal review if the activity is genuinely travel rather than ordinary conduct of your role from a foreign desk; however, your 42-day stay is work from another country, not business travel, and requires the full approval process.

Recommendation — not company policy: Raise your request in MosaicOne under 'Work from another country' with exact dates (3 November to 14 December 2026) and your workspace address, and file a Tax & Legal review request at least 21 calendar days before departure.

Recommendation — not company policy: Confirm with IT Security that your travel laptop meets encryption and VPN requirements, and notify them of your destination at least 5 business days before departure.

Next steps:
- Submit approval request to your director (Dana) and Tax & Legal via MosaicOne.
- Notify IT Security of your destination at least 5 business days before 3 November.
- Confirm your workspace address and planned work activities for the Tax & Legal review.

citations.heading_path: Working Outside Your Home Country > Eligibility
citations.snippet: Employees must have completed at least 12 months of continuous service to work outside their home country. The requirement applies to temporary work abroad, not to business travel: attending a customer site or a trade show on company business is governed by the Travel Policy and carries no tenure requirement.
A stay of more than 30 consecutive days in another country requires a Tax & Legal review before travel begins.

Germany, Ireland, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, Canada and Mexico are approved destinations for temporary work abroad. tools.name: search_policy_documents
tools.description: Semantic + lexical search over the 14 HR policy documents. Returns ranked chunks with the ids and heading paths a citation needs, each carrying the chunk's full text as well as a 320-character snippet, so a hit can be quoted without a second call; text is null on a hit marked quarantined, which carries its snippet only. Use get_policy_section for the sections AROUND a hit (include_neighbors) or for a section no search returned. topic prioritises one corpus topic; when the topic alone yields fewer than k hits or a single document, results are backfilled from the whole corpus.

query.description: The question, in the user's words.
query.title: Query

doc_ids.description: Restrict the search to these doc_ids.
doc_ids.title: Doc Ids

topic.description: Prioritise one corpus topic. When the topic alone yields fewer than k hits or a single document, results are backfilled from the whole corpus.
topic.title: Topic

min_dense_score.description: Minimum DENSE score (dense_score = 1 - cosine_distance). Applied to the full fused candidate list, then the top-k is taken from the survivors. Never applied to rrf_score, whose maximum is ~0.033.
min_dense_score.title: Min Dense Score

SearchHit.description:
One ranked chunk, carrying every field a citation needs (R2.5) and the chunk itself.

`text` is the stored chunk, clamped to `CHUNK_MAX_CHARS`; `snippet` stays the 320-character
display subset a citation shows a reader. It is `null` — and `quarantined` is `true` — for a
chunk the §7.4 injection shield has quarantined, because a chunk whose text gives the assistant
orders must not be readable in the model's own context.

output_schema.description:

`topic_backfilled` is `true` when at least one returned hit came from the unfiltered search the
soft `topic` filter runs underneath itself, and `backfill_reason` says what triggered it. They
move together: a widening that added nothing reports `false`/`null`, exactly as a search that
passed no `topic` does.

hits.text:
No employee may work outside their home country for more than 90 days in a rolling 12-month period. The 90-day figure is a company limit and is
independent of any shorter limit imposed by the destination country's immigration rules, which always take precedence.

Days are counted as calendar days of presence, including weekends and company holidays that fall inside the trip. A trip that begins on 3 November and
ends on 14 December counts as 42 days.

Separate trips inside the rolling window are added together. An employee who spent 55 days abroad in March and April may take no more than 35 further
days before the March allocation begins to roll off.
